title: Erdős #38: Essential Components and Density Boosting
description: Does there exist a set B that is NOT an additive basis but still has the density-boosting property: for any set A with Schnirelmann density α, some translate A ∪ (A+b) achieves density ≥ α + f(α)?

meta.author: Erdős (posed), OPEN
prerequisites: Essential components in additive number theory
meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries. Previously cited axiom names have been removed from the Lean source. The 'axiomatized' status reflects that the main result is not yet fully formalized in Lean.

overview.historicalContext:
This problem connects two fundamental concepts in additive combinatorics: Schnirelmann density and additive bases. Schnirelmann density σ(A) = inf_{N≥1} |A ∩ {1,...,N}|/N is a worst-case density measure, crucial in the study of additive number theory.

Erdős proved in 1936 that additive bases of order k have a specific density-boosting property with factor α(1-α)/(2k). Linnik in 1942 constructed an 'essential component' - a set that increases Schnirelmann density when added - that is NOT an additive basis.

This problem asks whether the stronger density-boosting property (improving counts for specific translates) can exist without being a basis. It probes the gap between 'essential components' and 'additive bases'.
overview.problemStatement:
Does there exist B ⊆ ℕ which is NOT an additive basis, but for every set A with Schnirelmann density α and every N, there exists b ∈ B such that |(A ∪ (A+b)) ∩ {1,...,N}| ≥ (α + f(α))·N where f(α) > 0 for 0 < α < 1?

**Status**: OPEN - neither existence nor non-existence proven.
overview.text: Does there exist a set B that is NOT an additive basis but still has the density-boosting property: for any set A with Schnirelmann density α, some translate A ∪ (A+b) achieves density ≥ α + f(α)?
overview.proofStrategy:
The formalization defines:
1. **Schnirelmann density** as the infimum of |A ∩ {1,...,N}|/N
2. **Additive bases** of order k (every n is a sum of ≤k elements from B)
3. **Density-boosting property** for translates A ∪ (A+b)

The known related results — Erdős's 1936 theorem (bases have the property), Linnik's 1942 construction (essential components exist that aren't bases), and the optimality of α(1-α) for B = ℕ — are recorded only as documentation comments, not as Lean axioms or theorems; they are not formalized in this file. The only Lean declaration is `erdos_38_conjecture`, an honest `Classical.em` disclosure that the open problem is decidably true-or-false.
keyInsights: **Schnirelmann density**: Unlike asymptotic density, it's the INFIMUM over initial segments - sensitive to early gaps
**Additive basis**: B is a basis of order k if every integer is a sum of ≤k elements from B (e.g., squares are order 4)
**Essential component**: Weaker than basis - just needs to increase density when added to any set
**The gap**: Erdős asks if the density-boost property (even stronger than essential) can hold without being a basis
**Known**: Bases have density-boost; some non-bases are essential components; unknown if non-bases can have density-boost
prerequisites: Essential components in additive number theory

sections.title: Problem Statement and Background
sections.summary: States the open Erdős Problem #38: does there exist $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that is NOT an additive basis, yet for every set $A$ of Schnirelmann density $\alpha$ some $b \in B$ boosts $|(A \cup (A+b)) \cap \{1,\dots,N\}|$ by a density-dependent factor $f(\alpha)>0$? Linnik (1942) built a weaker essential component that isn't a basis.
sections.mathContext: Schnirelmann density $\sigma(A) = \inf_N |A\cap\{1,\dots,N\}|/N$; an additive basis of order $k$ satisfies $B+\cdots+B$ ($k$ times) $=\mathbb{N}$, and Erdős's 1936 inequality bounds the density gain by $\alpha(1-\alpha)/(2k)$ for genuine bases.

conclusion.summary: We formalize Erdős Problem #38, which asks whether the density-boosting property for translates can exist without being an additive basis. The problem probes the gap between 'essential components' (which can fail to be bases) and the stronger translate-based density improvement.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: This problem is fundamental to understanding the structure of additive bases.

A positive answer would show that density-boosting is genuinely weaker than being a basis. A negative answer would give a new characterization of additive bases.
openQuestions: Does the density-boosting property imply being an additive basis?
What is the optimal function f(α) for additive bases?
Are there natural examples of essential components that fail density-boosting?

mainTheorems.name: schnirelmannDensity
mainTheorems.description: Defines the Schnirelmann density of a set A ⊆ ℕ as the infimum of |A ∩ {1,...,N}| / N over all N ≥ 1.

mainTheorems.name: countingFunction
mainTheorems.description: Counts the number of elements of A in the initial segment {1,...,N}, i.e. |A ∩ {1,...,N}|.

mainTheorems.name: IsAdditiveBasisOfOrder
mainTheorems.description: States that B is an additive basis of order k, meaning every natural number is a sum of at most k elements of B.

mainTheorems.name: IsAdditiveBasis
mainTheorems.description: States that B is an additive basis of some finite order.

mainTheorems.name: translate
mainTheorems.description: Defines the translate A + {b} = {a + b : a ∈ A} of a set A by a natural number b.

mainTheorems.name: boostsCount
mainTheorems.description: States that some b ∈ B makes the counting function of A ∪ (A + b) on {1,...,N} at least (α + f(α))·N, where α is the Schnirelmann density of A.
mainTheorems.leanType: (B : Set ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop

mainTheorems.name: HasDensityBoostProperty
mainTheorems.description: States that B has the density-boosting property for every set A and every N ≥ 1 with respect to the boost function f.

mainTheorems.name: Erdos38Problem
mainTheorems.description: Formalizes Erdős Problem #38: existence of a set B that is not an additive basis yet has the density-boost property for some f positive on (0,1).

mainTheorems.name: erdos_38_conjecture
mainTheorems.description: Records the (classically trivial) decidability that Erdős Problem #38 either holds or fails, marking the underlying question as open.

crossReferences.description: Problem #37 on essential components and lacunary sets is the companion problem. Both concern the density-boosting properties of specific sets in additive combinatorics
Problem #35 on Schnirelmann density is the foundation. Essential components (Problems #37-38) study which sets can boost the Schnirelmann density of any set with positive density
Additive bases (Problem #28) and essential components (Problem #38) are related: an essential component can convert any set with positive density into a basis
